start.text: An old woman sits among half-mended nets, fingers working a knot that never quite finishes. She hums without a tune.
Over, under, round the gull… over, under…

who.text: Who… I mend. That's who. Over, under.
Her eyes slide across you as if you were weather. Only when your ember comes close do her hands slow, for a breath.

lantern.text: A big one. With a lantern. Tollen shoulders, the Tollen walk. North, into the thick of it.
Said he'd come back for his name when he was done with it. Laughing, he was. Not sad.
I thought that was strange. I remember thinking it was strange. Over, under…

knot.text: The cord in your palm ties itself, loop by slow loop. Hesk's fingers stop.
That's the first knot. The founding knot. Gran's gran's gran tied the first Saltmarrow net with that, when there was nothing here but gulls.
My hands have lost it. Everyone's hands have. Only that string remembers now.

start_lit.text: Beacon-light falls gold through the loft slats. Hesk's fingers work the same knot, a little slower. She looks up once, toward the headland.
Is it midwinter? Someone's lit the gull. Over, under, round the gull…

start_knot_burned.text: Beacon-light falls gold through the loft slats. Hesk sits with a net across her knees, hands still, turning a cord over and over.
I've forgotten what I was mending. There was a knot. There was always a knot.
